title: Proxy-layer scaling-signal attenuation and cold-start priming plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a region-wide capacity event we observed persistent under-reaction from the HPA/KEDA autoscaling stack for the proxy-fronting inference pods. Symptoms included delayed scale-ups during short bursts and apparent false-negative KEDA triggers driven by high-percentile latency spikes being masked by transient proxy burst smoothing. This ticket captures the postmortem findings, immediate mitigations applied, and the action plan to reduce cold-start exposure and signal attenuation in the proxy layer.

Impact: Several customers on Dedicated tiers experienced elevated tail latency and request queuing for up to 9 minutes during bursty traffic windows. The platform remained available (no total outage) but SLA latency SLOs were violated for 4 customers.

Scope: affects inference proxy tier (edge-proxy service) + KEDA scalers wired to Redis stream triggers that feed HPA for runtime workers. Investigation spanned logs, proxy metrics, KEDA trigger logs, and Cloud metrics for node allocation and GPU warm pools.
root_cause: The proxy implements an internal 95th->50th percentile smoothing buffer to reduce upstream noise; during a bursty pattern this smoothing suppressed short high-percentile spikes that KEDA relied on for trigger thresholds. In combination, HPA's short stabilization windows and an overly aggressive cold-start penalty for warm-pool reclamation caused the worker pool to under-scale (false negatives). Two contributing factors: 1) proxy smoothing window configuration is too wide relative to burst duration (30s smoothing vs 5-15s bursts), and 2) KEDA scaler config used a percent-based threshold with a 60s cooldown that missed rapid spike-driven demand.
timeline: 2026-02-18T02:12Z - First customer alert: tail latency spikes observed in us-west-2; automated oncall routed to infra oncall.
2026-02-18T02:25Z - Initial mitigation: increased proxy logging and enabled temporary verbose KEDA debug. Rapid analysis showed smoothing filter reducing apparent 95th percentiles.
2026-02-18T02:40Z - Applied emergency change: reduce proxy smoothing window from 30s to 6s for affected service cohort (hotfix).
2026-02-18T03:05Z - Observed partial recovery: KEDA triggers fired more reliably but some warm-pool contention remained, delaying new worker initialization by ~30s.
2026-02-18T03:30Z - Enabled short-lived synthetic 'primers' that issue lightweight inference calls to warm pools to keep GPUs from reclaiming; reduced cold-start penalty observed.
2026-02-18T04:20Z - Post-incident monitoring: latency and scale behavior returned to baseline; began retrospective notes and action item creation.
mitigation: Immediate mitigations executed during incident: 1) reduced proxy smoothing window to 6s for the impacted proxy cohort, 2) lowered KEDA scaler cooldown from 60s to 20s for critical inference triggers, 3) launched synthetic primer traffic to warm GPU pools during burst windows, and 4) temporarily increased HPA max replicas by 30% to reduce queuing. These reduced customer impact while we designed longer-term fixes.
action_items: ENG-564101: Implement adaptive proxy smoothing (Mateo Ruiz) - make smoothing window adaptive based on observed burst duration; deliver prototype in 2 sprints.
ENG-564102: KEDA scaler configuration templates (Aisha Patel) - add burst-friendly presets that use short cooldowns and percentile-aware thresholds; add to runtime-1.26 release notes.
ENG-564103: Warm-pool priming subsystem (SRE team) - formalize synthetic primers with rate-limiting and per-customer opt-in; estimate 3 points.
ENG-564104: HPA stabilization review (Platform) - audit stabilizationWindowSeconds and tolerance settings across clusters; low-risk rollout plan by 2026-03-21.
ENG-564105: Observability dashboard (Observability eng) - add proxy smoothing telemetry and KEDA trigger hit/miss counters; alerting rule for >3 missed triggers in 10m.
ENG-564106: Runbook update (Oncall) - add steps for detecting smoothing attenuation vs true drop in traffic and quick rollback commands; owner: Maya Chen.
followups: Measure: run A/B for adaptive smoothing vs static in one region for 2 weeks and compare scale reaction time and false-negative rate.
Policy: update Dedicated SLA playbook to include rapid warm-pool priming during burst windows.
Design: evaluate replacing percent-based KEDA thresholds with hybrid token-rate model tied to request queue depth.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Added initial analysis and assigned to Mateo. I reproduced the smoothing effect in staging by replaying traces; confirmed 95th suppressed to near-mean when smoothing>20s.
2026-02-22 - Mateo Ruiz: Hotfix PR merged to reduce smoothing window. Need to iterate on adaptive smoothing — initial design doc attached.
2026-03-01 - SRE Lead (Maya Chen): Warm-pool priming worked well but caused minor cost overhead; will instrument cost metrics before enabling globally.
2026-03-08 - Product (Elena Novak): Customers want guarantees for sustained bursts; recommend adding a Dedicated policy for guaranteed burst headroom.
